mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate below 5% for three consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 shows two consecutive quarterly declines
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% signals contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a broad-based weakening in demand, which depresses corporate earnings and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline monthly
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of dual-trigger episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A positive monthly change in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 50,000 combined with an unemployment rate below 5% signals a strong labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate held constant at or below 3% for six consecutive months during a period of above-trend GDP growth (GDPC1) signals accommodative monetary policy supporting economic expansion, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS <= 3.0% for six months AND GDPC1 above previous 4-quarter average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase of over 2% in real personal savings (RSAFS) combined with a decline in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) signals a shift from spending to saving, which typically precedes a slowdown in demand and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly change > 2.0% AND GDPC1 monthly change < 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
